title: Lesson 50: General Systems Architecture: AI Governance, Model Risk, Compliance, and Audit Trails
description: How to govern AI systems you build and buy: model risk, tiering by harm, the NIST AI RMF functions, and the audit trail that makes a model reconstructable and defensible.

questions.question: Pre-launch testing is not sufficient as a governance control for an AI system. Why?
options: Model behavior stays fixed after ship, so a single sign-off is enough
Its behavior drifts as data or the vendor's version changes over time
Reviewing lower-risk systems is prohibited by regulation
Model outputs stay correct in production however they were tested
questions.explanation: A model is not stable after ship: its output distribution shifts as the data or the vendor's version changes, so governance needs ongoing monitoring as part of the structure, not only a pre-launch check.

questions.question: Which set names the four functions of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.explanation: The framework organizes AI risk work into Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage, run as a continuous loop rather than a single pass. Govern establishes accountability and policy, Map names context and failure modes, Measure evaluates risk, and Manage acts and feeds findings back.

questions.question: A complete evidence set for reconstructing an AI incident must align which records on the same event?
options: The system-action log, the AI interaction record, and the approval record
The vendor contract, the subscription invoice, and the product marketing brief
Only the final text sent to the customer, with no surrounding context
The encryption key status and the storage tier of the data
questions.explanation: A complete evidence set needs all three: the platform log of system actions, the AI record of the model's reasoning and retrieved context, and the human's approval, aligned on the same event so a past failure can be reconstructed.
